To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cell cycle response of small-cell lung carcinomas to VP16 is heterogeneous and that this heterogeneity is not due to differences in doubling times.
the sensitivity of a panel of SCLC cell line to VP16-induced G2/M and G1/S arrest is dose-dependent, and that the SCLC cell cycle response is heterogeneous.

the development and validation of a novel in vitro cell cycle assay for the prediction of clinical response to cytotoxic drugs.

the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of SCLC, and the identification of molecular markers of drug sensitivity that will facilitate the development of more-effective combination chemotherapy regimens.
the development of novel therapeutic approaches for small-cell lung cancer.
